body.query: Recent corporate action announcements by The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE: PG): reverse stock split, CUSIP or identifier change, redemption, or ticker change
body.systemPrompt: You are scanning a watchlist for an investment operations team. Report the most recent corporate action announced for The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE: PG), either by the issuer itself or in an official exchange or SEC notice: a reverse or forward stock split, a CUSIP or ticker change, a name change, an ADS ratio change, or a redemption, tender offer or exchange offer for this security. Ignore every other company and every other security. Ignore earnings, dividends, buybacks, share offerings, lawsuits, law-firm advertisements and analyst commentary. If no such action appears in the sources, write none found for event_type and not stated for every other field. Copy dates and times exactly as the source writes them. Write not stated for any field the source does not give. Never infer.

identifier_in_source.description: Ticker or CUSIP of the affected security exactly as the source prints it, or not stated

event_type.description: One of: reverse split, forward split, CUSIP change, ticker change, name change, ADS ratio change, redemption, tender offer, exchange offer, other, none found

terms.description: Split ratio, or redemption price and amount, as stated

effective_as_stated.description: Effective date and time exactly as the source writes it

effective_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the first trading day on the new terms for a split, or the redemption date for a bond, or not stated

new_identifier.description: New CUSIP or new ticker as stated, or not stated

source_notice_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD printed on the notice itself

## FAQ

 What security is Procter & Gamble (PG) removing from NYSE listing? 

 Procter & Gamble is removing its 3.250% Notes due 2026 from listing and registration on the New York Stock Exchange LLC under Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act. 

 Which form did Procter & Gamble (PG) and NYSE use for this delisting? 

 The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25, a Notification of Removal from Listing and/or Registration under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, for Procter & Gamble’s 3.250% Notes due 2026. 

 What regulations govern Procter & Gamble (PG) notes’ removal from NYSE? 

 The removal of Procter & Gamble’s 3.250% Notes due 2026 is stated to comply with 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(b) for exchange action and 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(c) for voluntary withdrawal by the issuer. 

 Who certified the NYSE action on Procter & Gamble (PG) notes? 

 The filing is signed on behalf of New York Stock Exchange LLC by Anthony Sozzi, identified as Analyst, Market Watch, certifying reasonable grounds to file Form 25 for the 3.250% Notes due 2026. 

 Does the Form 25 affect Procter & Gamble (PG) common stock? 

 The Form 25 specifically addresses 3.250% Notes due 2026 of Procter & Gamble. It refers only to this class of debt securities and not to Procter & Gamble’s common stock or other securities.

Neither reviewed 2026 dividend notice announces a new share split. This guide verifies no 2026 or 2027 split ratio or stock-distribution date. A cash-dividend increase changes cash per eligible share; a forward split changes how the same ownership is divided into units. The events should be tracked separately.

A hypothetical 2-for-1 split doubles share count while halving the theoretical price. Per-share dividend comparisons then need a matching adjustment. At a hypothetical $160 price before any such event, the $4.354 unchanged-rate scenario implies approximately 2.72% yield. results.title: Procter & Gamble CLO Sells 2,238 Shares in Tax Cover
highlights:
Susan Street Whaley, Chief Legal Officer and Secretary of Procter & Gamble Co, filed a Form 4 on August 24, 2026, reporting the sale of 2,238 shares of common stock on August 20, 2026, to cover taxes on a stock award.
...
- Shares sold: 2,238 shares of Procter & Gamble common stock disposed of on August 20, 2026, via transaction code S.
- Sale price: $143.79 per share, according to the filing.
- Purpose: The filing notes the shares were "sold to cover taxes on Stock Award."
- Direct ownership after transaction: 26,988.9685 shares held directly following the reported transaction.
- Indirect ownership: 7,187.9174 shares held indirectly by a retirement plan trustee.
- Reporting person role: Susan Street Whaley is identified as Chief Legal Officer and Secretary of Procter & Gamble Co.
...
According to the Form 4 filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Susan Street Whaley, serving as Chief Legal Officer and Secretary of Procter & Gamble Co (NYSE:PG), reported a single open-market sale transaction dated August 20, 2026. The filing discloses that 2,238 shares of common stock were disposed of at a price of $143.79 per share. The filing's footnote states the transaction was a sale "to cover taxes on Stock Award," indicating the disposition was associated with a tax obligation arising from a equity compensation event rather than a discretionary market sale.

Following the reported transaction, the filing shows Whaley directly holds 26,988.9685 shares of Procter & Gamble common stock. In addition, the filing reports 7,187.9174 shares held indirectly through a retirement plan trustee. No derivative securities transactions were reported in Table II of the filing. The Form 4 was signed by Wednesday Shipp as attorney-in-fact for Susan Street Whaley and filed on August 24, 2026.
...
The filing discloses a disposition of 2,238 shares of Procter & Gamble common stock by Chief Legal Officer Susan Street Whaley on August 20, 2026, at $143.79 per share, for the stated purpose of covering taxes on a stock award.
